summary: Tenzin Dorjee is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Lobsang Tsephel and Geshe Sonam Rinchen. He worked as a translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and served as General Secretary at Pullahari Monastery.

Tenzin L. Mullin is a scholar in religious studies and Japanology. Mullin completed a Master of Arts at the University of Otago under the supervision of Elizabeth Guthrie and primary supervisor Erica Baffelli.

Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Geshe degree from Menri Monastery and the Dialectic School, where he served as director (~1986–1989), and later founded Ligmincha Institute and Ligmincha International.

Ter Ellingson is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison before serving as a professor of music at the University of Washington (1981–2016).

Terese Tse Bartholomew is a specialist in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and sinology. She earned an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles, and served as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco.

Terrell Carver is a scholar in philosophy and related fields. He studied at Columbia University and the University of Oxford before holding academic posts at the University of Liverpool (~1974–1979) and the University of Bristol (~1979).

Terry Kleeman is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He completed his studies at the University of British Columbia (~1981–1988) and became a professor at the University of Colorado Boulder around 1998.

Terton Sogyal (1856–1926) was an active figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Patrul Rinpoche, and later taught prominent figures such as the 13th Dalai Lama.

Teruji Ishizu (1903–1972) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tohoku University, serving as dean and president (1963–1966), and later served as president of Miyagi University of Education.

Tessa J. Bartholomeusz (1958–2001) was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied at Florida State University and the University of Virginia (PhD), later teaching at Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis and Florida State University.

Tessa Verney Wheeler (1893–1936) was a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. She was educated at Addey and Stanhope School from 1905 to 1911 and at University College London between 1911 and 1914.

Tetsuei Sato (1902–1982) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He served as a professor at Taisho University and Gifu Kyoritsu University (~1971–1974), and was named professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (~1971–1982).
Tetsuhiko Shibata is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued his education at Taisho University. During his studies, he was taught by Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

Tetsujiro Inoue (1856–1944) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo, Heidelberg, and Leipzig, he served as professor and dean at the University of Tokyo, and as president of Daito Bunka University.

Tetsuo Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Waseda and Komazawa universities. He held multiple leadership positions at Komazawa University, including president (2002–2006), and later served as president of Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).

Tetsuo Yamaori is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University, where he later taught (~1973–1982), and served as a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~1988–1997).

Tetsuro Noguchi (1932–2022) was a scholar specializing in sinology, religious studies, and history and archaeology. Over his academic career, he held positions at Yokohama National University, the University of Tsukuba, and J. F. Oberlin University.

Tetsuro Watsuji (1889–1960) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He served as professor of ethics at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo.

Tetsuzo Tanikawa (1895–1989) was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He completed his education at the Kyoto University Faculty of Letters (~1919–1922) and later held academic posts at Doshisha University and Hosei University.

Teun Goudriaan is a scholar in the fields of Indology and religious studies. His academic career includes an appointment at Utrecht University, where he is attested as having served as Professor Emeritus.
